subject: crab
reasoning:

For the skeleton, I'm placing a root body joint and building the carapace from a scaled sphere flattened and widened to look shell-like. Defining the claw arm paths...

For the claws and limbs, I'm assuming chain() auto-generates parented joints along a path and just proceeding with that assumption to keep things coherent, planning the color palette next—burnt orange shell, darker legs, cream belly.

Finalizing color constants, then setting up helper functions for scaled ellipsoid geometry and outward-pointing cones built from rotated cone primitives, before starting the main build function.

Modeling the crab body: placing the carapace, belly, and rostrum as separate shell-colored parts anchored to a body joint, then adding jointed eye stalks with small cylinders positioned and rotated outward on each side.

Working through the eye geometry placement so the stalks, eyeballs, and pupils sit correctly, then sketching out the leg structure as segmented chains with four joints per side sweeping down to a foot tip.

Now I'm defining the arm chains similarly, with paths for shoulder-to-wrist movement and sweep radii for the limb thickness, figuring out how to attach hand parts near the wrist joint without explicit bone references.

For the pincer hands, I'm shaping the palm as an ellipsoid at the wrist and crafting the fixed and moving pincer fingers from rotated cone geometries, working out the splay angle so the two fingers pinch inward toward each other on the correct side.

Still placing geometry pieces... I'll also add a few small spine cones along the carapace's front edge for extra detail, keeping it minimal.

Now I'm adding a small tail fan and telson segment at the back of the abdomen, and checking how the legs and belly height relate to ground level so the crab stands properly.

For the eye joints I'll attach them via named joints parented to the body, and set up the meta export with the model's name and description. I don't need the rng import since no randomness is required here—I'll just finalize the part-building helper and write the complete code, passing model-space coordinates and bone references only where needed for the body and eyes.
